description: Machine-readable gate definitions for AES-P1.3 (SUE-440). Prose form: quality-gates.md. Engine: scripts/lib/quality-gates-core.mjs. Severity — reject: blocks materialization. fix: must be resolved before review. flag: human judgement required. Most gates below are driven by this file's own `patterns`/thresholds; a few (`implementation: "code"`) are structural checks — duplicate-paragraph detection, thesis/title word overlap, a frame-field presence check — that cannot be expressed as a regex pattern and are hardcoded in the engine instead. Those entries exist here so this file remains a complete registry of every gate id, but the engine does not read a `patterns` array for them because none exists; see each entry's `rationale` for why, and quality-gates.md for the same note in prose.

gates.name: prompt-echo
gates.rationale: The instruction given to the generator was emitted as prose. Observed in the SUE-417 fixture as both the dek and the first body line.

gates.name: duplicate-paragraph
gates.rationale: Fires when a normalised paragraph of ≥40 characters appears more than once in the body. This is a whole-document comparison across every paragraph pair, not a single regex a paragraph either matches or does not — expressing it as a `patterns` entry would misrepresent how the check works. Implemented directly in scripts/lib/quality-gates-core.mjs (the '--- G-02 duplicate paragraphs' block).

gates.name: scaffolding-leak
gates.rationale: Planning notes, placeholders, or template markers shipped as content.

gates.name: headline-thesis-fidelity
gates.rationale: Compares the content-word overlap between `article.frame.thesis` and `article.title`, below a two-word floor. This reads a structured field (`frame.thesis`), not the rendered body text a `patterns` regex runs against, and computes a set intersection rather than a match — not expressible as a pattern. Implemented in scripts/lib/quality-gates-core.mjs (the '--- G-04 headline fidelity to thesis' block); see quality-gates.md for why its scope is deliberately narrow.

gates.name: citation-integrity
gates.rationale: Provenance pointing at a disposable working document is not provenance. Duplicate citations to one URL inflate the apparent evidence base.

gates.name: filler-phrase
gates.rationale: Openings and closings banned by voice.md. They occupy the two positions in a piece that carry the most weight.

gates.name: overclaim
gates.rationale: Absolute or certainty-asserting language that the evidence rarely supports.

gates.name: empty-hedge
gates.rationale: A hedge with no number and no citation states nothing. 'We do not know X' is precise; 'results may vary' is filler.
patterns: (다양하게 나타날 수 있다|경우에 따라 다를 수 있다)

gates.name: formulaic-sectioning
gates.rationale: Generic section framing applied mechanically rather than earned by the argument.

gates.name: uncertainty-present
gates.rationale: Fires when `article.frame.uncertainty` is absent or empty. A presence/length check on a structured field, not a body-text pattern match — there is no prose for a regex to run against. Implemented in scripts/lib/quality-gates-core.mjs (the '--- G-11 uncertainty present' block).

evidenceDensity.name: evidence-density
evidenceDensity.rationale: Fraction of body paragraphs carrying a number, a date, or a citation marker. Below this the piece is assertion rather than analysis.

sequentialSummary.name: sequential-summary
sequentialSummary.rationale: Most citing paragraphs draw on exactly one source and the sources appear in order — the shape of a source-by-source restatement rather than a synthesis.

protectedSpans.rationale: What a polish pass may never alter. This is what distinguishes polish from rewrite, and it is why no rule in voice.md takes the form 'vary sentence length to sound natural'.
